steps.title: Prepare culture samples in well-plates
steps.instruction: Add phytoplankton culture and a parylene-coated stir bar (VP 711D-1, V&P Scientific, INC) to the wells of a plate to ensure thorough cell re-suspension.

substeps.instruction: For 96-well plates: pipette 300 µL of culture into each well.
For 24-well plates: pipette 2.8 mL of culture into each well.
Ensure the culture sample depth is 3.8 mm in both plate types.

steps.title: Acclimate and mix samples
steps.instruction: Acclimate the samples and ensure uniform suspension before measurement.

substeps.instruction: Acclimate samples at 16 °C and 120 µmol m-2 s-1 for a minimum of 10 minutes.
Mix the well-plates on a Cooke Microtiter Micro Mixer for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence time course
steps.instruction: Monitor chlorophyll a fluorescence from the top of the well-plate using a spectrofluorometer (Molecular Devices SpectraMax Gemini EM).

substeps.instruction: Set excitation to 445 nm and emission to 680 nm.
Position the plate so the distance from the photodioded fluorescence detector to the top of the culture is ~2 mm.
Measure fluorescence from the central region of each culture well repeatedly over a determined time course.

steps.title: Export and process raw data
steps.instruction: Export the generated .txt file from the spectrophotometer (Molecular Devices, SpectraWorks) to a Dropbox directory for processing.

substeps.instruction: Manually enter culture sample meta-data into the SinkingCulture_Catalog.csv data sheet using Microsoft Excel.
Import raw data and process using the SinkWORX data analysis pipeline in R-Studio Software Version 0.99.486.
Use the 'segmented' package for break point analysis and 'ggplot2' for plotting.

steps.title: Scale fluorescence data
steps.instruction: Scale the relative fluorescent units (RFU) to minimize variation caused by differences in initial cell suspension density.

substeps.instruction: Scale the initial even suspension (Elapsed Time = 0) to an RFU of 1.
Scale the final RFU plateau (when cells are resting at the bottom 3.8 mm below the surface) to 0.

steps.title: Calculate sinking rate
steps.instruction: Estimate the scaled sinking rate (s, min-1) and convert it to a standard sinking rate.

substeps.instruction: If an initial increase in fluorescence is observed (due to NPQ relaxation in the first 30 minutes), plot the square root of scaled RFU versus elapsed time.
Fit the data with a segmented linear regression to separate the initial rise phase from the sinking phase.
Extrapolate back to the y-intercept and rescale this intercept to 1.
Multiply the scaled sinking rate by the actual distance travelled (culture depth of 3.8 mm) and convert the value to meters d-1.
